findings.breaking_input: /arc-hunt invoice" ; touch pwned ; echo " (or a niche containing $(...) or a backtick). $ARGUMENTS is substituted textually into a double-quoted bash string before the shell parses it.
findings.why: A niche with a double quote, `$(`, or a backtick closes or expands the quoted string, and the shell runs the rest. The project's own rule forbids backtick and `$` inside a double-quoted embedded string. The allowed-tools prefix `Bash(node .claude/scripts/discover/arc-discover.mjs:*)` does not stop injection after the quote. Phase 01 will feed this argument into a miner that makes network calls.
findings.fix: Don't interpolate $ARGUMENTS into the command line. Have the command write the niche to a file with the Write tool and pass `--niche-file <path>`, or pass it via an env var with a single-quoted heredoc. The CLI should also validate the niche against a strict grammar and refuse anything else with exit 2.
findings.twin_of: hostile text interpolated into a shell, eval or yaml string

findings.breaking_input: Remove "discover" from the CATALOG array while any other "discover" string stays in arc-products.mjs (a comment, a lookup table, an error message). `grep -q '"discover"'` still passes.
findings.why: The grep matches anywhere in the file, not inside the CATALOG array, so it can pass without the catalog entry. This is the vacuous-pass class, and there is no negative arm for it unlike the room and policy checks.
findings.fix: Extract the CATALOG array with node (or a regex anchored on `const CATALOG = [`) and assert membership. Add a mutant arm that runs the same check on a copy with the entry removed and asserts it fails.
findings.twin_of: a test that passes proves the assertion held, not that the code ran

findings.breaking_input: Run the test where `$ARC_ROOT/processes` is missing or unreadable, or ARC_ROOT is wrong, so `ls` fails. `grep -c` then counts 0 lines of empty input and prints "0", and the trailing `|| true` swallows the failure.
findings.why: The check passes vacuously: it never asserts that `processes/` was listed. A scan that cannot read its input reports a clean result, which is the opposite of `COULD NOT SCAN`.
findings.fix: First assert `[ -d "$ARC_ROOT/processes" ]` and that it holds at least one `*.process.yaml` (14 today). Then check for a `discover*` file with `compgen -G` or a glob instead of `ls | grep`.
findings.twin_of: (g) a scan that cannot read its input reports `COULD NOT SCAN`, never an empty result

findings.breaking_input: `node .claude/scripts/discover/arc-discover` (no extension), or `node -` with the script on stdin. argv[1] is then a path that does not exist as given.
findings.why: `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` throws ENOENT synchronously at module top level. The CLI dies with a stack trace and exit 1 instead of the documented exit 2 refusal. The guard only protects against a missing argv[1], not an unresolvable one.
findings.fix: Wrap both realpath calls in a try/catch that falls back to false, or compare resolved paths via a helper that never throws.
findings.twin_of: (a) realpath-both-sides main guard in `arc-discover.mjs` and every CLI-shaped file
